title: Extremal quasimorphisms for the 3/4 family are out of reach of the obvious computation
body:
## What goes wrong

The values of scl(w_n) are already rigorous, being exact rational linear
programming. What is missing is the dual object: an explicit extremal
quasimorphism certifying the lower bound, which is the point of the side project.

`scallop -train -sup` is the mode that produces an actual counting quasimorphism
with its defect. For w_3 it returns 1/2 at word length 3 and at 4, so length at
least 5 is needed, and length 5 does not finish under GLPK in reasonable time. The
required length appears to grow like n + 1, because the quasimorphism has to see
the whole block a^n. So the cost grows exponentially in exactly the parameter that
indexes the family, and the naive route gives certificates for no member of it.
author: danny
what_was_tried:
`scallop -train L` (a rigorous lower bound from a genuinely different algorithm,
using train tracks) was run and is already sharp for w_3 at L = 4, confirming the
value independently. But that is an scl computation, not a quasimorphism, so it
does not produce a certificate.

`scallop -train -sup L`, which does produce the quasimorphism, was then run: L = 3
and L = 4 give only 1/2 for w_3, and L = 5 does not terminate under GLPK. The
pattern of where `-train L` becomes sharp -- L = 4 for n = 3, L = 5 for n = 4,
L >= 6 for n = 5 -- suggests L = n + 1 is needed throughout.

Two routes out, neither taken. `trollop -L filename` dumps the `-sup` linear
program as a sparse matrix and vectors; solving that in exact rational arithmetic,
or merely verifying a guessed dual point, would give the coefficients of the
extremal counting quasimorphism directly, and given the L = n + 1 pattern those
coefficients should be supported on words of the form a^k b and should be a visible
function of n. Alternatively a better LP solver than GLPK might simply finish.

The more promising route is not a certificate at all: since scl(w_n) is linear
fractional in the twist parameter, the surgery machinery should prove both bounds
for the whole family at once.

The numbers here come from a computation carried out in an AI agent session in
August 2026 using `scallop`, in its rigorous exact-rational mode, and spot-checked
against two independent algorithms. **No person has checked it.** Treat it as
computational evidence and not as established fact.
